patches.value: Use one Fourier coefficient representation Coeff = ℤ → ℂ, with MemH s the summability of (1+k²)^s |f_k|², and hn its square-root sum. It is the specified completion of Fourier polynomials, not a strengthened solution space. HB includes MemH, so totalized real tsums never certify regularity by themselves. Source homogeneous norms delete frequency zero. RealField is f(-k)=conj(f(k)); ZeroMean is f(0)=0. Product is coefficient convolution. S has multiplier exp(i t k³); inverse derivatives kill zero. The four terms of Htau, including its finite 1/τ coefficient, are copied exactly; numerical uses ordinary finite function iteration without cutoff. Time integrals are coefficientwise complex Bochner interval integrals. ContH explicitly gives norm continuity on the closed interval. Weak is the coefficientwise distributional time derivative, tested against compactly supported smooth real scalar functions; EssBound includes measurability, Sobolev membership almost everywhere and finite essential supremum. XPath uses weak derivatives; Xnorm uses essential suprema, while UB and SupH use continuous representatives. Piecewise records a finite set of breakpoints with smooth pieces and globally continuous spatial Sobolev paths; derivatives at finitely many joins have no effect on Weak or Xnorm. KSol is the integrated twisted Fourier equation, equivalent for continuous L² paths to the distributional physical equation by Fourier testing; no second physical Lean representation is introduced. Exact adds uniqueness and uniform H^s approximation by solutions with Fourier-truncated data. T013 supplies a checked weighted lp₂ realization only as reusable Hilbert-space infrastructure for truncation, inclusions and completion; FromLP is an explicit invertible positive Fourier weight, not an assumed capability. The pinned lp parameter 2 is the ℝ≥0∞ summability exponent (not a regularity index); real Sobolev order s stays in the weight. iteratedDerivWithin uses a natural derivative order and the actual closed interval. n2 is the maximum of pairwise minima (second largest magnitude), n3 the minimum of pairwise maxima (third largest), including ties. N in cutoff/high is a real frequency threshold, not an integer index. Nat L,n are step counts/indices and their real casts are explicit. E003-E005 keep the factor sqrt(2π) in source norms; E004/E005 quantify an admissibility threshold for positive epsilon, with constants chosen after epsilon and before time/input data. Each constant existential is outside the data, time-grid and Fourier-support quantifiers it must be uniform over. Original T,gamma,R and H001-H003 are unchanged and universally closed by the interface parameters; all E ports retain their full source signatures. Background notes remain optional references, never premise ports. Estimates, completion, reflection, endpoint matching and all operator-extension properties remain proof obligations; the header proves none. The plan has twelve distinct source-output steps, one shared Sobolev implementation bridge, and four independently usable subarguments; source paragraph coverage is explicit in each step.
